key_insight: Personal Visual Context Learning (Personal VCL) enables Large Multimodal Models to use a wearer’s own first‑person visual context at prompt time to answer personalized queries, enabling on‑the‑fly personalization without costly re‑training.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between generic LMMs and truly personal assistants by allowing models to disambiguate and reason about visual information unique to an individual (continuous first‑person streams) at inference time.
method: Formalize Personal VCL as the prompt‑time capability to incorporate user‑specific visual context for personalized queries and define an evaluation protocol.
Provide a modular prompt‑time approach: select/retrieve relevant frames from a wearer’s visual memory, ground references in those frames, and feed the grounded context to an LMM.
Evaluate the approach with tasks that test disambiguation, identity/scene recall, and personalized reference resolution from first‑person visual streams.
impact: Makes wearable and assistive LMMs more useful and responsive to individual users by enabling real‑time, privacy‑aware personalization at inference time—reducing the need for extensive per‑user fine‑tuning.

paper_title: Personal Visual Context Learning in Large Multimodal Models
paper_authors: Zihui Xue, Ami Baid, Sangho Kim, Mi Luo, Kristen Grauman
